question: In the reordering-sign study's fermionic model (swap rule s = -1, one-parent births of a parity knot, block readers with fixed real readings), which schedules of creations and births give the full three-detector (n-detector) contradiction, why did its prediction P7 fail, and does the result survive a different choice of each scaffold?
forbidden_inputs: No code of the predecessor or of its referee is imported; their receipts are read only for the gate's comparison. No sign pattern, phase or postselection enters a preparation except the start-sign patterns of P5, which are the variation under test.
primary_observable: Full contradiction with fixed readings: every even-size correlation <F_T Z_rest> is +-1 and T -> c(T) is not a character; exact match of the n-reader target table on all 4^n cells.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Depth-first schedules; the complex flip F3; unmatched reader conventions; the 7 other pair sign rules; s = e^{i theta}; listing changes (gauge).
first_executable_signal: Time the n = 3 gate against the predecessor's verify_fock.json before any fresh case.
resource_budget: One process, exact integers, at most 720 commit orders, 4,610 schedules, 4,096 reader assignments and a combinatorial count of 7,484,400 schedules; expected a few minutes, under 2 GiB.
stop_rule: Stop after the gate and P1-P8.
decision_or_followup_rule: If P2 at n = 5, 6, P3 and P4 hold, record the sign as a property of the supplied schedule relative to the real reader convention and STOP the order line unless a native rule fixing the schedule is named; otherwise report what the sign depends on beyond the relative order.
nonclaims: No claim about physical fermions, exchange statistics as distinct from one CZ per crossing, physical time, a second growth round, or weightings other than the uniform ones named.
